today_bh: A clear link needs a BH-adjusted p-value below .05: the Benjamini–Hochberg correction allows for testing 13 signals at once. It changes the p-values only; the lines are ordinary 95% intervals, not widened for it. So an interval can stay clear of zero and still miss the corrected threshold: “Load of 400+ two days ago” (interval +0.05 to +0.66, BH-adjusted p = .114).
lever_bh: A clear link needs a BH-adjusted p-value below .05: the Benjamini–Hochberg correction allows for testing 18 rows at once. It changes the p-values only; the lines are ordinary 95% intervals, not widened for it. So an interval can stay clear of zero and still miss the corrected threshold: “Drank alcohol” (interval −0.54 to −0.11, BH-adjusted p = .057).
factors_conclusion: 2 of 13 tracked signals have a clear link: went to bed 1 h+ later than usual (−0.46) and slept 1 h+ less than usual (−0.43). Both are about disrupted sleep.
